source.title: Stochastic Training of Residual Networks: a Differential Equation Viewpoint
source.authors: Qi Sun; Yun-Zhe Tao; Q. Du

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether adding dropout reduces held-out error, using a modified dropout placement in PreResNets on CIFAR-10.
record.gate_note: The paper also discusses optimizer and batch-size effects and cites other studies, but reports no new experiment testing those claim versions. Its one-dimensional loss-landscape examples are illustrative; they do not measure trained-network generalization gaps or sharpness.
record.test_reason: The study compares modified Bernoulli dropout against no dropout in three PreResNet depths on CIFAR-10, directly testing V6 through held-out classification error. It is not an original source for V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors interpret stochastic residual networks through stochastic differential equations and backward Kolmogorov equations, with noise acting as artificial viscosity. Their CIFAR-10 experiments show lower held-out error and reduced training–inference discrepancies with suitable dropout; toy examples illustrate excessive-noise fitting problems. Determining the optimal noise level for network depth and structure remains open.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Bernoulli dropout in a modified PreResNet, placing one dropout layer after the last convolution in each block and scaling retained activations during training; evaluates the plain network at inference.
record.method_sensitivity: CIFAR-10 validation error varies with dropout survival probability and network depth. The authors state the optimal probability depends on depth and structure.

fits_no_version.finding: The one-dimensional examples show noise smoothing the loss landscape, excessive noise impairing fitting, and batch sizes 3 versus 6 changing SGD trajectories; they report neither held-out batch-size effects nor magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Injected noise can smooth a toy classification objective and alter optimization trajectories, with excessive noise impairing data fitting.

record.problems: Only CIFAR-10 is tested, with standard data augmentation; reported table values are means of 4 runs. Standard error bars are shown in figures but their numeric values are not provided in the text. No very-small-training-set condition is tested.
record.rows_left_out: None. Table 1 reports 21 model-by-survival-probability validation-error entries, all included.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers and tuning-dependent generalization.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, empirical underfitting from excessive dropout in image classifiers, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized versus random training examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All table values are means over four runs on the 10,000-image test set, which the prose also calls validation. Parentheses report best-run errors. Figure 6 is described as mean ± standard deviation despite the paper's inconsistent use of 'standard error'; numeric uncertainty is unavailable here. Remove the record's limits_scope verdict: suitable configuration is already part of V6, and untested clauses do not justify that label. The additional learning curves are declared as omitted, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Very small training sets; fully connected classifiers; data augmentation with dropout and weight decay jointly removed.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 PreResNet-20, -56 and -110; survival probabilities 85–97.5%; standard augmentation, weight decay 10^-4, and 164 training epochs.
relationships.reason: All dropout means are below their corresponding controls: 7.59–7.98% versus 8.22%, 6.19–6.43% versus 6.55%, and 5.58–5.88% versus 6.00% (R1–R21); statistical significance is not established.
relationships.display_finding: All tested dropout settings lowered mean test error relative to their matched controls, but statistical significance was not established.

tranche.reason: Modified Bernoulli dropout placement in residual blocks tests the same dropout-generalization question using held-out classification error.

reader_labels.reason: Each reported dropout validation error is lower than its p = 100% baseline (R1–R6, R8–R13, R15–R20).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10 PreResNets at the tested dropout probabilities
reader_labels.reason: The authors say improvement depends on suitable survival probability and that the optimum depends on network depth; the tested settings do not establish the small-training-set or joint dropout-and-weight-decay claims (R1–R20).
